title: Relock Loan-to-Value and Credit Score Pricing Grid — Builder Extended Rate Lock
content:
The relock of a Builder Extended Rate Lock is priced on a grid of the relock loan-to-value and the buyer's qualifying credit score.

**Rule.** The relock loan-to-value is the loan amount on the lock divided by the contract price on the Home Purchase Agreement the lock finances, as a percent. A lock whose relock loan-to-value is above 88 and whose qualifying credit score is below 720 adds 0.0625 percentage points to the relock fee percent; a lock whose relock loan-to-value is above 88 and whose qualifying credit score is 720 or higher adds 0.03125 percentage points; any other lock adds nothing. The points are added to the relock fee percent before that percent is applied to the loan amount on the lock.

## Grid

| | Qualifying credit score below 720 | Qualifying credit score 720 or higher |
|---|---|---|
| Relock loan-to-value above 88 | add 0.0625 points | add 0.03125 points |
| Relock loan-to-value 88 or below | nothing | nothing |

## Records read

- Loan amount and qualifying credit score: the lock record.
- Contract price: the Home Purchase Agreement record of the agreement the lock finances.

## Cases on both sides (hypothetical inputs)

- Loan amount USD 445000.00, contract price USD 500000.00: relock loan-to-value 89 percent, above 88. With a score of 700, 0.0625 points are added; with a score of 720, 0.03125.
- Loan amount USD 440000.00, contract price USD 500000.00: relock loan-to-value exactly 88 percent, not above 88; nothing is added whatever the score.
